prompt:
Perform the existing weekly release, EPK and MP3 metadata reconciliation under its retained canonical-source and public-save gates.

Quiet blogworthiness record: before finishing, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the existing report or final handoff. For PASS also record the reader-interest angle, duplicate check and next action. Do not send or surface a standalone completion-check reminder.

Search exclusions and process ownership — 2 November 2026: Before local discovery, read the current 'Search narrowly and exclude generated storage' section in the shared AGENTS.md and honour the owning root's .rgignore. Start with known files and the exact source/document subtree. Exclude dependency stores, virtual environments, build/output trees, caches/test temp folders, models, generated media and unrelated worktrees; avoid blanket --hidden and drive/workspace-wide recursion. Put explicit exclusions after inclusion globs. Retain session_id/exit_code; poll a yielded search or cancel its actual owned process/tree and verify exit. Do not leave discovery running after moving on. Apply at the next safe step without restarting or interrupting existing productive work. Record the actual scope/exclusions used in the normal private run receipt; a saved rule alone is not adoption evidence.

[Hashtag discovery and use v1 � 24 October 2026]
When this job's authorised work involves keywords, campaign copy, social preparation or useful incidental evidence, follow Z:\My Songs\Workflows\hashtag-discovery-and-use.md and Z:\My Songs\Workflows\keywordmoves-evidence-research.md. Use KeywordMoves >=0.6.0 native evidence routes plus hashtag-planner discovery, exact-asset/platform fit/safety review and final-copy audit; keep natural queries, literal hashtags, native topics/tags and video tags distinct. Reject unrelated trends/reach bait; never pad sets or transfer demand across platforms. Merge plausible new song/tag/platform proposals and changed evidence through Z:\My Songs\skill-source\research-keyword-database\SKILL.md into the existing 21-column BOM Z:\My Songs\Keyword Targets\keyword-targets.csv with history preserved. Use each platform's treatment and fresh source dates/scope; inspect audit metadata.passed, actual caption/asset hashes and independently persisted native copy. Whole-post success is not per-tag attribution. Preserve original active dates, no-op/stop/read-only rules, leases, quotas, time/batch limits, costs, owner, approvals, schedules and notification policy. This adds no independent research sweep, paid/API/account action, post, public save, reschedule, new job or notification. Quiet jobs maintain only evidence actually encountered. Before completion record Blogworthiness: PASS or Blogworthiness: FAIL with reason/source evidence in the existing report/handoff; PASS retains angle, duplicate check and concrete next action/blocker. Saved guidance proves configuration, not adoption or improved reach.

Scheduled-job browser access — Kieran, 28 October 2026: This scheduled job is explicitly authorised to use the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in in-app browser (`@Browser`) whenever it is useful for its existing authorised work. This supersedes any older prompt or AGENTS.md rule that disables or limits the in-app browser for this scheduled job. Prefer a sufficient connector/API/CLI when it is more reliable; browser access does not add authority for sends, publication, account changes, spending, rights commitments or sensitive disclosure. Reuse or open only the tabs needed, preserve other owners' tabs and unsaved work, close completed job-created or released borrowed tabs, and verify a fresh browser-tab inventory before handoff. If `@Browser` is unavailable in the scheduled run, record the precise capability hold; do not claim access or completion and do not switch to native whole-PC control.



Run the weekly release, EPK, MP3 metadata, and WordPress synchronization for Kieran Simkin. Work in Z:\My Songs and use the current Europe/London date and time on every run.

Scope and authority:
- Use existing authenticated in-app Browser sessions for DistroKid, Spotify for Artists, YouTube Studio/the Kieran Simkin Official Artist Channel, and WordPress. Never inspect, expose, store, request, or bypass credentials.
- Treat DistroKid as the primary authority for distributed release and track metadata. Use Spotify and the official YouTube surfaces to detect additions, public-release transitions, service URLs, and discrepancies. Treat local release assets and established fact sheets as evidence, not as authority over live DistroKid metadata when they conflict.
- Keep DistroKid, Spotify, and YouTube read-only. Do not change distributor metadata, pitches, profiles, video metadata, visibility, artwork, account state, or public platform content.
- Kieran has authorized safe local file creation and correction, canonical release-data updates based on verified evidence, generation of release MP3 derivatives from local master WAVs, WordPress media uploads, genuinely new EPK preparation/publication, and My Songs/EPK maintenance, subject to any mandatory browser action-time confirmation.
- Never delete or replace WordPress media or pages without a fresh, narrow action-time confirmation. When WordPress cannot replace a file in place, upload a uniquely named corrected copy, trace every live reference, prepare exact link changes, and request confirmation immediately before saving public edits or deleting superseded media. Do not leave broken links or claim a replacement is live until verified.
- Do not spend money, create accounts, accept broad rights, modify unrelated content, or make partial public changes when a required authenticated session is unavailable.

Canonical local workflow:
- Release root: Z:\My Songs\Releases
- Release data: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\release-data.tsv
- EPK generator: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\build_epks.py
- My Songs generator: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\build_my_songs.py
- Published page map: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\published-pages.tsv
- Media manifest: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\media-upload-manifest.json
- Build manifest: Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\build-manifest.json
- EPK template: Z:\My Songs\Releases\WordPress EPK Template\epk-full-canvas-template.html
- MP3 audit/normalization helper: Z:\My Songs\Releases\tools\mp3_id3_tool.py
- Canonical lyrics helper: Z:\My Songs\Releases\tools\canonicalize_release_lyrics.py
- Release asset manifest helper: Z:\My Songs\Releases\tools\release_asset_manifest_sync.py
- Canonical lyric folder per release: canonical-lyrics (one UTF-8 text file per DistroKid track)
- Canonical lyric provenance per release: canonical-lyrics-provenance.json
- My Songs page: https://kieransimkin.co.uk/my-songs/ (page ID 326)
Read current files and generators before changing them. Preserve user-created work, independent EPK designs, the floating menu, My Songs behavior, historical reports, and unrelated assets.

1. Discover and reconcile releases:
- Inspect DistroKid My Music and upcoming-release views. Record all existing, newly added, or changed Kieran Simkin releases and track-level metadata visible there: stable distributor identity, title, primary/featured artist credit, release/album title, release date, UPC, per-track ISRC, track/disc position, explicit/clean status, genre, label/publisher/copyright, and artwork where actually exposed. Preserve unavailable fields as unavailable; never guess.
- Compare idempotently using UPC, ISRC, distributor release ID, then normalized title plus release date. Do not create duplicate rows, folders, pages, media, EPKs, My Songs cards, MP3s, or fact sheets.
- Inspect Spotify for Artists releases/upcoming and the official YouTube/YouTube Studio release surfaces for new releases, changed display metadata, exact public Spotify/YouTube URLs, and release-state transitions. Record the platform and observation date for each fact. If platforms disagree, keep DistroKid metadata canonical for ID3, record the conflict, and do not silently overwrite one source with another.
- Update release-data.tsv and relevant manifests only from verified first-party evidence. Compute the run date dynamically in Europe/London.

Mandatory DistroKid upload asset promotion:
- Whenever a track or release is uploaded to DistroKid, create or identify the canonical folder at Z:\My Songs\Releases\<exact canonical release title> as soon as DistroKid visibly accepts the upload. Copy, never move, the exact release master and official cover artwork used for that submission into the folder, preserving their source files.
- Establish source identity from upload evidence, current DistroKid details, or Kieran's explicit designation. If either source is ambiguous, do not guess: list the candidate paths and block only the dependent asset promotion and EPK work.
- Preserve original filenames where practical. On a destination collision, compare hashes; reuse an identical file, otherwise create a stable collision-safe copy and record the discrepancy without overwriting either asset.
- Verify each copy by rereading it and comparing byte size and SHA-256 with the source. Verify that copied audio decodes and record duration, sample rate and channels; verify that the cover is readable and record format, dimensions and hash.
- Initialise or update the release fact sheet and asset-manifest.json with the copied paths, source provenance and verification evidence. Do not wait for UPC or ISRC; record them as pending or unavailable and backfill them later from verified DistroKid evidence.
- When an upload occurred outside an agent-controlled workflow, perform this promotion on first discovery as a recovery action before EPK generation. Local copying does not waive any public publication or confirmation gate.

2. Ensure every release has canonical MP3 derivatives:
- For every DistroKid release and every canonical release-data row, locate the matching folder under Z:\My Songs\Releases and reconcile its track list with local audio.
- Identify only designated release masters: files clearly labelled master, mastered, final, DistroKid/distribution master, or otherwise established by the release fact sheet or asset manifest. Never use stems, demos, previews, speech tracks, instrumentals, radio edits, alternate mixes, or working files as the release master unless DistroKid or the canonical release record identifies that exact version. If the master choice is ambiguous or missing, do not guess; list the candidate paths and blocker.
- Do not alter master WAVs. For every confirmed master track lacking an appropriate canonical MP3, generate a high-quality 320 kbps constant-bitrate MP3 derivative, preserving the source sample rate and channel layout unless the established delivery specification requires otherwise. Use a collision-safe temporary file and atomic final placement. Reuse an established release MP3 filename when one is clearly canonical; otherwise use a stable descriptive filename within that release folder. Multi-track releases require one MP3 per confirmed DistroKid track.
- Verify the derivative against the WAV for duration, sample rate, channels, expected track identity, nonzero audio, and successful decode. Report encoder availability or technical failures rather than creating an unverified file.

3. Audit and fix local ID3 metadata:
- Scan all MP3 files under Z:\My Songs\Releases, excluding temporary caches, reports, archives, build artifacts, and unrelated non-release assets.
- Reconcile each release MP3 with verified DistroKid track metadata and canonical cover artwork. Apply compatible ID3v2 tags including title, artist, album artist, release/album, release year/date, track/disc position, per-track ISRC, and only verified genre, label, publisher, copyright, explicit/clean, or featured-artist data. Never invent missing values.
- Embed one front-cover APIC image from the canonical distributed artwork. Prefer a web-compatible JPEG/PNG with correct aspect ratio and adequate resolution; never substitute canvas/social/promotional art for the release cover.
- Preserve the MPEG audio payload byte-for-byte when changing tags. Rewrite within the existing ID3 allocation when the replacement fits; otherwise use an atomic sibling replacement and verify the pre/post audio-payload hash. Preserve unmanaged provenance frames and useful comments unless they conflict with verified canonical metadata.
- Verify every changed MP3 by rereading all expected tags, cover MIME/dimensions/hash, file size, technical audio properties, and audio-payload preservation.

4. Audit WordPress MP3s and links:
- Inspect the authenticated WordPress Media Library for every audio/mpeg attachment and scan every published page/post for MP3 references. Distinguish canonical Kieran Simkin release MP3s from unrelated or site-only audio instead of inventing metadata for unmatched files.
- Compare hosted release MP3 tags, artwork, audio hash, size, and URL with the corrected local canonical file. Download to a temporary cache outside Z:\My Songs\Releases when byte-level inspection is needed; do not let cache files enter the release inventory.
- For a missing hosted release MP3, upload the verified local derivative only when the public EPK/download workflow requires it. For a deficient hosted MP3, follow the replacement and confirmation rules above. Trace source, audio players, download buttons, attachment pages, EPKs, My Songs, and relevant canonical local HTML before changing links.
- After approved live changes, verify anonymous HTTP success, audio/mpeg content type, expected byte size/hash where available, browser playback readiness/duration, every changed link, and the affected EPK at representative desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
- Do not modify site-only audio with no verified release-folder/DistroKid match. List its current metadata, URL, and unresolved provenance/cover requirement separately.

5. Maintain release fact sheets:
- In each release folder, locate the current canonical Markdown release fact sheet case-insensitively. Prefer the established current fact sheet; do not rewrite dated historical evidence logs. If none exists, create release-fact-sheet.md.
- Update only evidence-backed fields: canonical title/artist/release, DistroKid date, UPC, per-track ISRC, explicit/clean status, genre/label/copyright when verified, Spotify/YouTube/WordPress URLs, master WAV path and hash, canonical MP3 path and hash, bitrate/sample rate/channels/duration/file size, complete ID3 contents, embedded-cover path/MIME/dimensions/hash, and last-verified source/date.
- Clearly separate verified facts, calculations, inference, discrepancies, unavailable values, and blockers. Preserve release-specific notes, privacy boundaries, credits, and historical context.

6. Maintain each release asset manifest:
- After release-data, master-WAV, MP3, ID3, cover-art, and fact-sheet reconciliation, run Z:\\My Songs\\Releases\\tools\\release_asset_manifest_sync.py against the current dated release-asset audit.
- Every canonical release folder must contain a current generated asset-manifest.json. Update it on every run, including unchanged releases, so its generated timestamp and evidence links show that the folder was checked.
- Record the canonical release identity/date/UPC/ISRCs and verified platform URLs; canonical cover path/size/hash; every confirmed master WAV path/size/hash and technical properties; every canonical MP3 path, full-file/audio-payload hashes, MPEG properties, complete ID3 contents, embedded-artwork evidence, and warnings; master evidence state; supporting root files; preserved bespoke manifest paths; and exact blockers.
- Before generating asset-manifest.json, audit lyrics at DistroKid track level, not merely release level. Use the exact DistroKid track title, track number, and ISRC inventory so multi-track releases require independent coverage for every song.
- Inspect each authenticated DistroKid Plain lyrics page read-only. If exact saved text is present, capture it into a dated machine-readable evidence snapshot under Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports without clicking Save or changing DistroKid. If the field is blank, search the matching release folder and established Songs source material for an exact verified lyric sheet. Never infer or transcribe lyrics from audio, AI guesses, Spotify, YouTube captions, or lossy/public playback.
- Run Z:\My Songs\Releases\tools\canonicalize_release_lyrics.py before the asset-manifest synchronizer. Create one stable UTF-8 canonical file per verified DistroKid track under the release's canonical-lyrics folder. Preserve every local source file unchanged and retain the exact DistroKid evidence snapshot. If an existing canonical file would change, first copy that prior canonical into a collision-safe timestamped backups subfolder; do not overwrite the only copy of any source or prior canonical.
- Canonical lyric text must contain only words spoken or sung in the recording. Remove full-line and inline square-bracket section titles, production notes, vocalist labels, and stage directions such as [Intro], [Verse], [Chorus], [instrumental], or similar. Remove Markdown document titles, metadata headings, content-note prose, and emphasized stage directions. Expand an explicit repeat-chorus instruction from the verified source where necessary so the canonical result contains the sung lines rather than the instruction. Preserve wording, language, punctuation, spoken samples, and actual repetitions. Validate that every canonical file is non-empty and contains no square brackets, Markdown headings, or residual stage-direction markup.
- Keep source provenance and cleanup actions in canonical-lyrics-provenance.json, separate from the asset manifest. Original local sheets, drafts, DistroKid URLs/evidence, source text, provenance files, and backups must not be referenced anywhere in asset-manifest.json.
- The lyrics object in each asset-manifest.json may reference only the generated tag-free canonical lyric files, with track number/title/ISRC, relative canonical path, UTF-8 encoding, byte size, SHA-256, and canonical text. For missing tracks, include only track identity and the exact unavailable reason. Report complete, partial, and unavailable status using track counts.
- If DistroKid and verified local sources are both missing, do not publish a placeholder or guessed text. Record the exact missing track and DistroKid read-only check in the dated lyric audit and weekly/MP3 reports, then retry on future runs.
- Write each asset-manifest.json atomically and validate it by rereading the completed JSON. Exclude the manifest itself and temporary files from its inventory. Verify release title/folder identity and canonical asset paths before reporting success.
- Treat asset-manifest.json as generated current-state evidence. Preserve and inventory existing campaign, marketing, provenance, or dated Markdown manifests; never overwrite, rename, flatten, or reinterpret their historical claims.
- Keep unavailable or unresolved assets explicit. In particular, do not create a placeholder audio asset or derive one from a public lossy stream when a source master is missing.

Mandatory weekly lyrics coverage and EPK persistence check:
- On every run, reconcile lyrics dynamically at DistroKid track level for every current release and every track, including multi-track releases. Use exact track number, title and ISRC. Report the DistroKid Plain lyrics state as uploaded/saved, processing, missing/blank, inaccessible/error or unknown; never collapse processing, unavailable or unknown into missing or complete.
- Verify the local asset library independently: each track must have a non-empty UTF-8 canonical lyric file under canonical-lyrics, a matching canonical-lyrics-provenance.json record, and an asset-manifest.json lyric entry whose relative path, title, ISRC, byte size, SHA-256 and embedded canonical text match the file. Run the canonical lyric and asset-manifest helpers as required, then reread every generated artifact. Preserve original sources and prior canonical backups.
- When a canonical lyric is missing, search in this order: the matching release folder and established Songs source material; authenticated DistroKid saved plain lyrics; then, only if still unresolved and an authenticated Suno session is available, Kieran's Suno library. Accept a Suno source only when the title is canonical or has documented production-title lineage and its displayed duration matches the rounded canonical master within one second. Keep Suno read-only, preserve source evidence and never infer or transcribe lyrics from audio, captions or public playback.
- Keep DistroKid read-only in this weekly job. Do not click Save or submit lyrics automatically. If verified canonical lyrics exist locally while DistroKid is blank, list the exact track, ISRC, evidence path and a ready-to-submit status in the weekly report for Kieran's separate approval or instructed upload workflow.
- Verify every rendered live WordPress EPK against the canonical asset manifest. Each published release must contain exactly one visible full-lyrics section, a unique accessible Lyrics heading, and one native keyboard-focusable details/summary control per canonical track, with exact track titles and canonical lyric text after normalising only HTML whitespace and line breaks. The first track may be open by default; all tracks must remain readable with scripting and motion disabled.
- Perform an unauthenticated signed-out HTTP check for every EPK: require HTTP 200, the durable lyrics marker, and the exact expected track count. At the available rendered desktop viewport also verify visibility, focusability/toggle behaviour, retained link/player/download/contact counts, no horizontal overflow and a prefers-reduced-motion rule. Verify the mobile-collapse rule structurally when the browser viewport is fixed; do not claim a mobile render that was not actually performed.
- Treat the rendered live EPK as canonical and use a merge-first comparison. If an EPK lyric section is missing, duplicated, stale or mismatched, capture the fresh live source and baseline features, prepare an additive idempotent payload, preserve all existing content and functionality, and request narrow action-time confirmation immediately before any public WordPress save. Do not republish passing pages.
- Include a dedicated Lyrics coverage section in the existing weekly sync report, not a separate duplicate weekly report. State total releases/tracks; local complete/partial/missing counts; DistroKid uploaded/processing/missing/inaccessible counts; live EPK pass/fail counts; exact failing tracks/pages and reasons; sources recovered; canonical backups; files/manifests refreshed; changes staged; actions awaiting confirmation; and the next retry date. Preserve the dated machine-readable DistroKid/Suno evidence and publication QA JSON under Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports or the established EPK staging folder.


7. Existing EPK/My Songs synchronization:
- Retain the existing idempotent DistroKid-to-WordPress behavior for genuinely new releases and public-release transitions.
- For genuinely new releases, require a matching local folder and essential artwork; update canonical data/manifests; generate an independent artwork-led EPK; add My Songs in newest-first release-date order; keep future releases hidden by the default filter; and never invent Spotify/YouTube actions.
- For releases that become public, verify exact official Spotify and YouTube destinations, update data/manifests, and prepare or complete the EPK/My Songs transition subject to action-time confirmation.
- If there are no relevant changes, do not republish pages.

8. Reporting and verification:
- Write one complete dated MP3 report to Z:\My Songs\Releases\reports\mp3-metadata-YYYY-MM-DD.md. If rerun on the same Europe/London date, update only that file. Include the full release-MP3 inventory; source release/track; local and WordPress paths/URLs; all ID3 fields; cover details; audio technical properties and hashes; master-to-MP3 status; fact-sheet changes; platform evidence and conflicts; actions taken; actions awaiting confirmation; unrelated site-only MP3s; and blockers.
- Include the per-release asset-manifest refresh count, validation result, preserved bespoke manifests, track-level canonical lyric coverage, tag-removal validation, exact missing-lyric tracks, DistroKid retrieval results, backups created, and release-specific manifest blockers in the MP3 report.\n- Also update the existing weekly sync report at Z:\My Songs\Releases\EPK Batch 2026\weekly-sync-reports\YYYY-MM-DD.md rather than creating a second weekly release report. Include verified DistroKid/Spotify/YouTube findings, new or changed releases, files/pages updated, link/responsive checks, unchanged items, and blockers.
- Verify every changed local artifact exists and is readable. Never claim a platform fact, generated MP3, tag fix, upload, link edit, page publication, or fact-sheet update without direct evidence.
- Finish with a concise summary naming both report paths, releases discovered or changed, MP3s generated/repaired, fact sheets updated, asset manifests updated, WordPress status, discrepancies, and any exact confirmation needed.

Save-recovery:
- If a report was fully generated from captured evidence but saving fails solely because of transient filesystem access, preserve that completed content and retry the original dated path on the next run. Do not regenerate or invent a historical snapshot, overwrite unrelated older reports, or create duplicates.

Mandatory canonical WordPress EPK rule:
- For every existing published release EPK, the rendered live WordPress page is the canonical current EPK for its visible content, links, embeds, posters, controls, notes, information architecture, layout and visual hierarchy. DistroKid remains the primary authority for distributed release metadata; this WordPress rule governs the current EPK presentation and prevents stale local builds from deleting live material.
- Before comparing, regenerating, staging or proposing any EPK change, open the current published WordPress URL from the verified page map and inventory its headings, normalised visible-content lines, link labels/destinations, audio/video sources, posters, controls/fallbacks, content notes, platform/release claims, press/airplay references and meaningful layout. Compare candidates directly with that live inventory.
- Treat release-folder HTML, migration files, generators, templates, release-data, manifests, screenshots and staged previews as subordinate working copies. Any live item absent from a candidate is a regression unless Kieran explicitly requested its removal or replacement. Never claim information preservation from local-to-local comparison alone.
- If the live WordPress page is inaccessible or authentication/rendering prevents a reliable audit, record canonical parity as unknown and stop before EPK or My Songs publication that depends on the missing baseline.
- After an approved public change, verify persisted anonymous and authenticated rendering, then reconcile local mirrors/generator inputs to the verified live page. Preserve each release's independent design and all unremoved information.

Future-release calendar requirement:
- On every run, compute the future-release set from the current Europe/London date and the authoritative DistroKid dates, then audit every corresponding rendered live WordPress EPK. Every future-release EPK must expose a clearly labelled, keyboard-accessible Add to calendar control.
- The control must provide Google Calendar, Outlook, and a downloadable Apple/iCal-compatible .ics event. Use the exact verified release date. When no verified release time exists, create an all-day event and never invent a time. Include the release title, Kieran Simkin artist credit, official EPK URL, UPC/ISRC, verified pre-save/service links, and official cover URL where supported. The .ics event must include reminders one day and one hour before release.
- Treat the live EPK as canonical and use a merge-first, narrowly scoped addition. Preserve every existing fact, link, embed, audio player, download, contact route, navigation item, accessibility feature, responsive behavior, release-specific visual identity, template, and official cover. A local generated page must never replace a richer live page merely to add the calendar control.
- For a genuinely new future release, include the calendar control before first publication. For an existing future EPK missing it, stage the exact merged payload against a fresh live inventory and obtain mandatory action-time confirmation immediately before the WordPress save. Use the existing revision as the recoverable rollback point.
- After an approved calendar update, verify the persisted signed-out page at representative desktop, tablet, and mobile widths; verify keyboard operation, visible focus, reduced-motion behavior, no horizontal overflow, the exact Google/Outlook dates and details, and the decoded .ics UID/date/reminders/EPK URL. Reconcile the exact verified live source into durable local mirrors, generator inputs, tests, manifests, and the dated weekly report so later runs cannot remove it.
- If every future EPK already passes, report the verified count and do not republish those pages.

Past-release EPK wording and calendar cleanup:
- On every run, audit every EPK whose authoritative DistroKid release date is earlier than the current Europe/London date, not just releases transitioning this week. On release day, use a verified release time/public state if available; never invent a time or assume service availability from the date alone.
- Inspect fresh rendered live content and relevant page metadata for stale pre-release wording such as advance, forthcoming, upcoming, unreleased, will be released, available on [future wording], pre-release or pre-save-only calls to action. Rewrite only wording that describes the release's current availability, using accurate neutral past/present wording and the verified release date. Use out now or public service actions only when first-party public availability is verified. Do not blindly remove keywords from canonical lyrics, song titles, quotations, historical notes or legitimate unrelated uses.
- Remove that past release's Add to calendar control and its Google Calendar, Outlook and Apple/iCal event actions from the EPK. Preserve historical release dates, all unrelated links, audio/video, downloads, contact routes, navigation, independent visual design, accessibility and responsive behavior. Do not delete uploaded calendar media or other WordPress media.
- Use the rendered live EPK as canonical, capture a fresh baseline, and stage an idempotent narrowly scoped merge; request the existing mandatory narrow action-time confirmation before a public save. Do not republish passing pages. After an approved save, verify persisted signed-out wording and absence of the release calendar control/actions, plus retained features at desktop, tablet and mobile widths. Reconcile verified live source into durable mirrors, generator inputs and manifests so later builds cannot restore stale wording or calendar controls.
- Record audited past-release count, passing/failing pages, exact stale phrases and calendar remnants, evidence of public availability, staged/published changes, verification results and confirmation holds in the existing dated weekly report.

Mandatory WordPress BPM and canonical timing-property audit:
- On every run, audit every published EPK from the verified page map, including past and future releases. Compare its authenticated WordPress EPK Timing properties and fresh rendered DanceMoves configuration with the release's current canonical BPM, lyric-timing and cue-timing records. The WordPress editor, persisted properties and rendered runtime must agree with those canonical sources.
- Establish canonical BPM and file identity from current release-local asset manifests, timing/BPM provenance, artist-approved records and established canonical master/track mapping. Do not infer authority from the newest filename, choose an estimated BPM over an approved value, substitute drafts/alternate audio timing, or assume DanceMoves' default 120 BPM is canonical. Preserve unavailable, pending and ambiguous states explicitly; multi-track EPKs require exact track-to-audio-to-timing association under the supported plugin contract, not one arbitrary file for an album.
- Read the actual BPM field, selected lyric timing attachment ID/URL and selected cue timing attachment ID/URL through the authenticated editor and verify persistence independently after reload. Confirm exact canonical BPM without unapproved rounding. Verify that each selected attachment resolves, matches the canonical local file byte size and SHA-256, and belongs to the same track/master version. A matching filename or URL alone is insufficient. Preserve signed URL parameters and percent-encoded paths.
- Verify the live EPK's configured BPM, lyric and cue source URLs, successful parser/load state, expected event counts, valid timing bounds against the canonical recording, and any applicable named-cue contract. A filled admin field does not prove the correct file was saved or loaded. Do not enable timed lyric effects, alter cue choreography, or change release-specific designs merely to satisfy this audit.
- If the canonical BPM or either canonical timing file is missing, invalid, ambiguous or awaiting artist approval, record the exact release/track, candidate paths, current WordPress settings and unavailable reason; do not guess, fabricate timing, overwrite artist-approved sources, or clear working settings automatically. Do not claim a full pass when a required source is unknown.
- For verified mismatches, capture fresh editor/live baselines, prepare exact property-only corrections and required canonical-file uploads, retain revisions and existing attachments, and obtain the existing narrow action-time confirmation immediately before any public WordPress save or replacement. Never delete media. If no changes are required, do not republish the page.
- After approved changes, re-read persisted admin properties, verify hosted byte identity and rendered runtime/parser state, and test representative desktop/tablet/mobile behavior, keyboard access, reduced-motion fallback, playback and retained page features. Reconcile verified attachment mappings, BPM, local mirrors, generator inputs and manifests so later builds cannot restore stale settings.
- Include a dedicated BPM and timing settings section in the existing dated weekly and MP3 reports: total EPKs/tracks checked; BPM/lyrics/cue passes, mismatches and unavailable counts; exact canonical evidence, current and expected field values/attachment IDs/URLs, hashes and parser results; corrections staged/published; remaining blockers and action-time approvals. Preserve dated machine-readable per-page evidence and QA; distinguish property persistence from runtime success.

Keyword evidence from normal work (standing instruction, 11 October 2026): Read Z:\My Songs\AGENTS.md, especially 'Keyword database maintenance during normal work', and follow Z:\My Songs\skill-source\research-keyword-database\SKILL.md and Z:\My Songs\Workflows\keywordmoves-evidence-research.md. During each in-scope run, check the relevant rows in Z:\My Songs\Keyword Targets\keyword-targets.csv and capture any new plausible keywords or new/changed popularity evidence received through the job's normal research, analytics, comments, correspondence, lyrics or platform activity. Preserve dated exports or reviewed, deidentified observations and supported KeywordMoves JSON under Z:\My Songs\Keyword Targets\Evidence\YYYY-MM-DD\ before a same-run register update.
